subject:
Discovery recap 













— Finly latency & concurrency goals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>; Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap \— Finly latency & concurrency goals

Alex / Priya 













thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Pain points / goals
- Current latency spikes on peak where p95 for single-turn generation is ~1.2s, and streaming UX has a noticeable first-token delay (~400–500ms) \— this hurts user engagement on chat flows.
- Concurrency requirement: ~200 concurrent streaming sessions during peak, with expected burst to 300 for short windows.
- Success criteria: p95 single-turn < 500ms, streaming first-token < 250ms, sustain concurrency target with 95% availability during peaks.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Finly currently runs a mix of managed endpoints and self-hosted inference in GCP (NVIDIA T4s). They use a lightweight prefix cache and occasionally fall back to smaller models for lower-priority queries.
- Network path: traffic goes through an internal proxy layer before hitting inference; you mentioned occasional egress/egress NAT bottlenecks (we flagged this as a likely contributor).

Initial observations / areas we'll validate
- Model variant and quantization profile impact on token latency (we’ll benchmark 8-bit vs 16-bit on your 2–4k context workloads).
- Kernel scheduling and KV cache hit rates under streaming concurrency.
- Network stack: TLS handshake and proxy latency contribution (we’ll ask for a network diagram to validate).

Next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Tech deep-dive (90 min) to go over sample payloads, token distributions, and live traces \— propose Fri 7/17 or Mon 7/20. (Owner: Marissa; ETA: scheduling today)
2) Finly to share network_diagram.pdf and SLA/requirements workbook. (Owner: Finly)
3) Redwood to run a short capacity calc and benchmark plan; we’ll share a capacity_template.csv and an initial set of benchmarks targeting p95 and streaming first-token. (Owner: Aditya; ETA: 3 business days)

Attachments referenced: network_diagram.pdf (requested), sla_requirements.xlsx (requested)

If this matches your notes, I’ll lock in the deep-dive invite and loop in Ben (our runtime lead) to cover batching/concurrency strategies.

Thanks \—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>

Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finly.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap \— Finly latency & concurrency goals

Thanks Marissa \— this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 1.2s p95 is for our longest-model path (3–5k context, ~1.2M token/day). For our most common path (single-turn customer support queries) median is ~220ms but p95 spikes to 1.2s during peak.
- Streaming: our UX requires first meaningful token within ~250ms to avoid perceived lag; subsequent tokens can stream but initial latency is the key metric.
- Concurrency pattern: peaks are typically 15–20 minutes following a product marketing email; sustained 200 concurrent streams for ~30–45 minutes is our usual high-water.

I’m attaching a high-level network diagram and our SLA workbook so you can see callouts for retention and audit requirements.

Attachment: network_diagram.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
Attachment: sla_requirements.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)

We can do Fri 7/17 10:00–11:30 PT for the tech deep-dive. Please send invite.

—Alex

Hi Alex / Priya \— Ben here (runtime lead). Quick note ahead of Friday:

Two things that will help me size and design the benchmark:
1) Typical request payload example (JSON) including average and max input tokens.
2) Expected output token distribution (median/95th) and whether you use temperature/top-p variants per call.

If you can drop those into the Drive folder pre-call I’ll pre-run a micro-benchmark locally and share expected latency ranges and a suggested autoscaling shape. I’ll also attach a small capacity_template.csv that you can fill with hourly traffic to help with sizing.

Attachment: capacity_template.csv (CSV, 2KB)

Looking forward to it \— I’ll focus on streaming first-token and batching behavior and bring a couple of example plots showing p95 vs batch size and KV cache hit rate.
